dimensions.analysis: The candidate never asked the interviewer any spec-level question about batch-protocol.md ambiguities (cid reuse across attempts, whether ok records can be mixed with retries, transport response ordering guarantees). They asked once whether they were allowed to read the test file, which the interviewer answered trivially, but this is not resolving genuine ambiguity about the bug mechanism -- it is a permissions question. All later 'clarify' moments were the interviewer pulling information out of them via repeated prompts rather than the candidate proactively surfacing ambiguity.

The candidate never stated a mechanism before editing; they arrived at a location (the response loop in _dispatch_chunk, noticing outstanding never resets payload) through a long series of interviewer nudges rather than naming the actual defect (frame correlation by position vs cid) before touching the code. Even their pre-edit statement was 'maybe what we need to do is also reset payload here', which is a vague, partially wrong guess rather than a specific mechanism, and the actual fix (indexing outstanding instead of chunk) appears to have been arrived at without a clearly stated hypothesis moment.

Long stretches of reading and code review passed with minimal or fragmented narration, and multiple times the interviewer had to explicitly ask the candidate to narrate out loud or repeat the same question because the candidate had gone quiet or off-topic (including nonsensical filler like off-topic phrases). The transcript alone would not let an interviewer follow the reasoning path to the fix -- the interviewer had to actively drag it out via at least five separate re-prompts.

The actual code change made (switching chunk[position] to outstanding[position]) is a minimal, targeted edit that matches the real root cause and left the rest of the retry loop, backoff, and batching untouched. However the edit was reached without a clearly narrated prior plan, so while the change itself is competent and scoped correctly, it reads as landing on the right line by trial rather than by design.

The candidate ran the test suite immediately after the edit and confirmed a fail-then-pass transition, and when pressed by the interviewer they walked back through the fix specifically tracing r1/r2/r3/r4 through the outstanding list to confirm the ordering held after the fix rather than just accepting the green run. This post-hoc trace under interviewer pressure is a real verification act, though it was prompted rather than volunteered.

When pushed hard by the interviewer, the candidate correctly explained that responses were being matched positionally into chunk instead of the shrinking outstanding list, and walked through a concrete R1/R2/R3/R4 example showing why the original code corrupted R1 while leaving R3 unresolved -- this is a genuine, mechanism-level explanation of the root cause. However this reflection was entirely interviewer-extracted via three consecutive follow-up questions rather than self-initiated, and the deeper 'why it stayed invisible until a partial retry' framing was never articulated.
